sections.h2: What are the options for selling a house in Urbana?
sections.html:
Urbana sellers can hire an agent, go it alone, or sell as-is to a cash buyer. Tenants change the picture, because the city runs a rental registration program, and the University of Illinois next door keeps the rental market busy.

Urbana belongs to Champaign County, shares its western edge with the city of Champaign, and holds most of the university campus. The 2020 count was 38,336, and the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate is 39,719, up 1.9% from its 2020 base.

sections.h2: What do Urbana housing and households look like?
sections.html:
Five-year survey results portray a young, renter-heavy city where home values sit far under those in the Chicago suburbs.

  • Owner-occupied share of homes: 37.3%, so renters hold most of the stock
  • Middle value among owned homes: $184,900
  • Middle monthly rent including utilities: $972
  • 16,856 households of just under two people each (1.98)
  • Midpoint household income $45,346, with 28.0% of residents below the poverty line
  • Adults holding a four-year degree or more: 56.7%
  • Share who lived at the same address a year earlier: 72.8%
  • Trip to work: 14.2 minutes on average

Median age at the 2020 census was 27.2. The latest five-year survey tallies 10,569 renter-occupied units against 6,287 owner-occupied ones.

sections.h2: Why is Urbana mostly rentals, and what does the city require of landlords?
sections.html:
The city says it has more than 10,000 rental units, nearly two-thirds of its housing, and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign enrolls more than 50,000 students annually. The city adopted a Rental Registration and Inspection Program, described on its program page.

  • Every rental property must register each year and pay a fee from the city's schedule of fees.
  • The program year runs from October 15 to October 14, matching the leasing calendar.
  • It covers single-family homes, duplexes and multi-family buildings, including room rentals where the owner also lives there.
  • Nursing homes, hotels and motels, housing authority units and university-certified housing are excluded.
  • The city aims to inspect every rental on a cycle of three to five years, and results appear in its open data portal.

Landlords register through an online Citizenserve account, and the Building Safety Division answers questions at 217-384-2443. If you own a rental, make sure the registration is up to date before listing, and ask the division what the inspection record shows.

sections.h2: Who collects the property tax on an Urbana house?
sections.html:
The Champaign County Treasurer and Collector bills and collects it, from the Bennett Administrative Center at 102 E. Main Street in Urbana, phone 217-384-3743. The county mails a single bill for the full year with coupons for two equal installments, and does not send a second bill. The collector handles more than 77,000 real estate bills for 156 taxing districts, which include school districts, cities and villages.

Champaign County real estate tax calendar for 2026 bills
DateWhat happens
May 1Bills are mailed
June 3First installment due
September 3Second installment due
September 30, 4:30 p.m.Last day to pay by check, e-check or card; later payments are cash, money order or cashier's check
October 1A $10 cost is added to each unpaid parcel for notices and publication
December 1 to 31Advance payments accepted, from 50% of the prior year's total up to 10% over it

The treasurer's pages state that postmarks do not apply to the late-payment dates. All of the 2026 dates above have passed, and the same pattern repeats with new dates each year. If the county does not have your current mailing address, call the Supervisor of Assessments at 217-384-3760.

sections.h2: What exemptions and tax programs can an Urbana owner use?
sections.html:
The Treasurer's tax page lists the programs and the office that handles each one. Most go through the County Assessment Office at 217-384-3760, which is also the number for corrections to bill information.

  • Owner-occupied exemption
  • Over-65 exemption for real estate, and the Senior Assessment Freeze
  • Disabled persons exemption and various veterans exemptions
  • Natural disaster homestead exemption
  • Tax deferral for owners over 65, run by the County Treasurer

Before you sell, ask the assessment office what is on file for the parcel, so the buyer's first bill is not a surprise. Champaign County has also elected to acquire delinquent real estate taxes as trustee for the taxing districts, beginning with the 2025 taxes payable in 2026 (Public Act 104-0553), so the county, as trustee for the taxing districts, takes the delinquent taxes at the sale in place of private tax buyers. If back taxes are owed, get a payoff from the Treasurer before a closing date is fixed.

sections.h2: What shaped Urbana, and what do its neighborhoods offer?
sections.html:
Europeans first settled the area in 1822, calling it Big Grove. When Champaign County was organized in 1833 the county seat was set on 40 acres, and the name came from Urbana, Ohio. The Illinois Central line bypassed the town and ran two miles west, where West Urbana, later Champaign, grew around the depot.

The Urbana Free Library, founded in 1874, sits downtown. The Lincoln Square area hosts the Market at the Square each Saturday morning from May to November, running since 1979. East of downtown, the Candlestick Lane neighborhood, centered on Grant Place and parts of Fairlawn and Eastern Drives, lights its yards from the third Saturday in December through New Year's Day. Urbana uses a mayor-council form with seven wards.

NOAA normals for 1981 to 2010 show about 41 inches of precipitation and 23 inches of snowfall across a year, with extremes from 109 degrees in July to minus 25 in winter.

sections.h2: What do Urbana schools, roads and buses offer a buyer?
sections.html:
Urbana School District elementary schools are Leal, Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., Dr. Preston L. Williams Jr., Thomas Paine and Yankee Ridge, with an early childhood school on the Prairie Campus next to Williams. Urbana Middle School served 897 students in grades 6 to 8 as of 2024, and the current Urbana High School building dates to 1914. University Laboratory High School is a publicly funded lab school on campus and sits outside the district.

South of I-74 lies most of the city, with Lincoln, Cunningham and University exits. University Avenue is US 150 and Vine Street and Cunningham Avenue carry US 45. Local buses run through the Champaign-Urbana Mass Transit District, and University of Illinois Willard Airport serves the area.

sections.h2: Does an inherited Urbana house need the usual seller disclosure?
sections.html:
Not always. Illinois expects residential sellers to give the buyer a disclosure report ahead of signing (765 ILCS 77/20), but Section 15 exempts several kinds of seller, including a fiduciary administering a decedent's estate, a transfer from a decedent by will or intestate succession, and transfers made under court order.

Who signs the deed decides whether an exemption applies, so check with the closing attorney. The Champaign County Recorder can tell you the current deed requirements and fees before you schedule a signing.

faqs.q: Does the city of Urbana inspect a house before it sells?
faqs.a: The city's permit and rental pages describe permits and a rental inspection cycle. Call the Building Safety Division at 217-384-2443 to ask whether anything applies to a sale at your address.

faqs.q: What dates apply to Urbana property tax installments?
faqs.a: There are two installments, with bills going out May 1. For 2026 they fell on June 3 and September 3, and the pattern repeats yearly.

faqs.q: What should the owner of an Urbana rental do before listing?
faqs.a: Confirm that registration is current, because the program year runs October 15 to October 14 and fees are annual. The Building Safety Division can explain the inspection history, which also appears in the city's open data.

faqs.q: Where can an Urbana owner pay property tax in person?
faqs.a: Pay at the Champaign County Treasurer's Office, 102 E. Main Street in Urbana. A 24-hour drop box sits in front of the guard shack in the parking area, and cash, checks, money orders and cards are accepted, with cards and checks only through September 30.

faqs.q: How fast can a cash sale of an Urbana house close?
faqs.a: Once the title work, payoff letters and deed are ready. A cash closing depends on the buyer's funds, the title company and the county's recording of the deed.
